title: How Wi-Fi reaches your devices

steps.say: Wi-Fi is like an invisible whisper that your router sends through the air, so your devices can listen. Let's see how far it travels!
The router sends out radio waves in every direction, like ripples spreading out when you drop a pebble into a pond.
This laptop is close to the router, so the ripples reach it fast and strong. See all the signal bars? Quick and happy!
Now the phone is farther away, and there is a wall in the way. Walls soak up some of the waves, like a thick blanket muffling a sound. So the signal gets weaker.
The TV is the farthest, with another wall to cross. Only a tiny whisper of signal makes it all the way, so videos might stop and wait. That is called buffering!
Here is a trick: put the router in the middle of your home and away from thick walls, and the waves reach everybody better.

recap: Remember: Wi-Fi is invisible ripples. The closer you are and the fewer walls in the way, the stronger your signal.
question: Where in your house would you put the router, and why?
